info.title: anonymize API
info.description: Privacy-first PII redaction API. v1 contract.

intent.description: An unrecognized value is accepted and dropped (parsed as absent), never rejected with 400.

post.description: Anonymize text: detect PII spans and return the rendered `anonymized` field plus the structured spans for client-side customization. The optional `markerFormat` selects the render format; tier gating applies (Free: xxxxx/blackbar; paid tiers Docs/API/Pro/Ultra: also `default`; Pro/Ultra additionally: `custom`). Omit `markerFormat` to fall back to the caller's user-profile preference, then to the tier default. The optional `ambiguous` field controls how low-confidence detections (the UNKLAR/ambiguous layer) render in `anonymized`: `redact` (default) splices them in as `[UNKLAR_n]` — masked formats (xxxxx/blackbar) mask them exactly like any other span; `mark` inlines the original text alongside the marker as `[UNKLAR_n: original]`; `keep` leaves them as plaintext, the legacy behavior. `redact` is the default because uncertain detections used to reach every caller as plaintext regardless of tier — a leak this field closes; older or generic callers that omit it get the safe default automatically. `uncertainSpans` (offsets, category, score) is returned in ALL three modes, unaffected by this field. Its `id` is a per-category preview counter independent of the `[UNKLAR_n]` numbering in `anonymized` (that one runs under a single shared `UNKLAR` label) — correlate an `uncertainSpans[]` entry to its marker in the text (or vice versa) by `start`/`end`, which is exact and present in both regardless of mode.

401.description: Two distinct cases: (1) `code: 'turnstile_required'` — an anonymous request needs a Cloudflare Turnstile token (or a valid IP-bound verified cookie); signed-in and API-key callers never see this one; carries `message`. (2) `code: 'invalid_api_key'` — the Authorization header named a key that is malformed, unknown, or revoked; no `reason` (an attacker should not learn whether a key ever existed) and no `message`. Distinct from `account_tier_required` below: this is about the key itself, not the plan behind it.

402.description: Tier required. Two distinct cases: (1) `code: 'tier_required'` — the requested `markerFormat` is not available on the caller's tier (body adds `markerFormat`, `tier`); (2) `code: 'account_tier_required'` — the API key is valid, but the account it belongs to has no API access on the Free plan (body adds `tier: 'free'`, `channel: 'api'`). The key itself is not revoked - upgrading the account to Docs or above reactivates it.

413.description: Text exceeds the caller's tier char limit

422.description: `code: 'custom_rules_timeout'` — one or more of the caller's active custom rules exceeded the anonymize-time processing budget against this request's text (defense in depth: a pattern that passed save-time validation but still backtracks catastrophically at runtime). Fails closed — the request is rejected rather than silently completing with custom rules skipped. Review and adjust the offending custom rule(s); the response never names the pattern or request text.

post.description:
Anonymize a Word document (.docx, max 10 MB) or a PDF (.pdf, max 20 MB and 500 pages). The output is always rebuilt from scratch with all detected PII replaced by markers — only deliberately extracted content reaches it, so hidden data (comments, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects) is removed by construction, and no original content stream survives underneath a redaction.

**PDF input** is read through its text layer and returned as paragraphs and page breaks. Layout, tables, columns, headers/footers and images are NOT preserved — tables and columns come back as ordinary paragraphs in reading order, and every PDF response carries a `pdf_layout_flattened` warning saying so. A scanned PDF with no text layer is rejected (`no_text_layer`); there is no OCR.

Multipart upload with a `file` part, an optional `markerFormat` field (same tier gating as /anonymize), an optional `redactUncertain` field, and an optional `outputFormat` field. Send every field BEFORE the file part — fields after the file are not reliably parsed. Requires a paid plan (Docs and up); anonymous callers are rejected. Degradations (omitted footnotes, merged cells, flattened PDF layout, ...) are reported honestly in `warnings`.

`redactUncertain` is `"true"` | `"false"` (strict — any other value 400s), default `"false"`: when `"true"`, low-confidence detections are ALSO replaced in the output; either way they are always listed in `uncertainSpans` for review.

`outputFormat` is `"docx"` | `"text"` (strict) and applies to PDF input only. It defaults to `"text"` on the API-key channel and `"docx"` on the browser channel. With `"text"` the response carries the anonymized string instead of a file, pages separated by a form feed (`\f`, the pdftotext convention). A .docx upload has real structure to preserve and therefore has no text mode: asking for one returns 400 `unsupported_output_format`.

redactUncertain.description: Also replace low-confidence detections in the output. Default "false" when omitted.

outputFormat.description: PDF input only. Default "text" for API-key callers, "docx" for session callers. Rejected with 400 for .docx input.

200.description: Redacted document + span report, or — for PDF input with `outputFormat=text` — the anonymized text + span report. Which shape arrives is decided by `outputFormat`, so a client that never sends it always gets the one its channel defaults to.

400.description: Not a valid .docx or .pdf (`invalid_file`; PDF parse failures carry `reason: "INVALID_PDF"`), missing file part, `redactUncertain`/`outputFormat` sent as an unsupported value (`invalid_field`), or `outputFormat=text` requested for .docx input (`unsupported_output_format`)

401.description: Two distinct cases: (1) no Authorization header and no session cookie at all — files require an account, there is no anonymous upload; body is `{ error: { message: 'unauthenticated' } }`. (2) `code: 'invalid_api_key'` — the Authorization header named a key that is malformed, unknown, or revoked; body is `{ error: { code: 'invalid_api_key' } }`. No `reason` in either body.

402.description: Tier required: Free-tier callers (`required: 'docs'`), or the requested `markerFormat` is not available on the caller's tier

413.description: File exceeds the cap for its format (`file_too_large`, with the applicable `limit`), the PDF has more pages than allowed (`too_many_pages`, with `limit` and `actual`), or the extracted text exceeds the tier char limit (`char_limit_exceeded`)

422.description: Password-protected/encrypted document (`encrypted_file`), or a PDF with no text layer — a scan (`no_text_layer`). Neither is retryable, and there is no OCR path.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (shared daily budget with /anonymize)

503.description: Processing at capacity or inference unavailable — retry later

post.description: Request a magic-link sign-in email. Always returns 202 to prevent user enumeration.

patch.description: Update current user preferences (language, theme, marker format, custom marker map).

delete.description: Delete the current user account. Requires typing the account email address to confirm.

post.description: Create a new API key. The plaintext key is returned ONCE in this response.

402.description: Tier required: any paid tier (Docs/API/Pro/Ultra); body: `{ error: { code: 'tier_required' } }`

get.description: List active API keys for the current user (revoked keys excluded).

delete.description: Revoke an API key (soft-delete; the key is no longer accepted).

get.description: Current effective rate limits (reads from env vars, so self-hosted instances return their own configured values).

List custom redaction rules for the current user. Each rule defines a regex pattern that the anonymizer applies as a high-confidence span; matches override overlapping model detections. Open to all tiers including Free (a downgraded Pro user keeps their rows visible) - but rules stay DORMANT on Free: `/anonymize` skips them and re-upgrade lights them back up.

post.description: Create a custom redaction rule. Pattern must be a valid regex up to 300 characters; a ReDoS guard rejects pathological patterns. Gated to paid tiers: Free/unauth callers receive 402 `tier_required`. Per-tier quota: Docs/API 20, Pro 100, Ultra unlimited. A 503 `validation_unavailable` means the pattern itself was never assessed - the save-time validation worker didn't come up in time on our side; retry after the given `Retry-After` seconds.

402.description: Tier required: any paid tier (Docs/API/Pro/Ultra); body: `{ error: { code: 'tier_required' } }`

422.description: Pattern rejected (invalid regex, ReDoS guard, or quota reached)

503.description: Validation temporarily unavailable (`validation_unavailable`) - not a pattern rejection, a liveness failure on our side. `Retry-After` header set; retry the same request.

patch.description: Update an existing custom redaction rule owned by the current user. Gated to paid tiers; Free/unauth returns 402. A 503 `validation_unavailable` (only when `pattern` is included) means the save-time validation worker didn't come up in time on our side, not that the pattern was rejected; retry after the given `Retry-After` seconds.

503.description: Validation temporarily unavailable (`validation_unavailable`) - not a pattern rejection, a liveness failure on our side. `Retry-After` header set; retry the same request.

delete.description: Delete a custom redaction rule owned by the current user. Gated to paid tiers; Free/unauth returns 402.

get.description: List allowlist entries for the current user. Entries define terms that the anonymizer must never redact (matched as word-boundary literals, case-sensitive or insensitive per entry).

post.description: Create an allowlist entry. Gated to paid tiers (Docs/API/Pro/Ultra). Returns 402 with code tier_required for Free/unauth callers.

patch.description: Update an existing allowlist entry owned by the current user. Gated to paid tiers (Docs/API/Pro/Ultra).

delete.description: Delete an allowlist entry owned by the current user. Gated to paid tiers (Docs/API/Pro/Ultra).

get.description: Download a GDPR-style export of all data associated with the current account: user profile, auth providers, API keys, custom rules (plaintext patterns), allowlist entries (plaintext values), and recent sessions.
Current 24-hour rolling-window usage counter for the anonymize endpoint, scoped to the signed-in user.

post.description: Resolve the Fungies checkout-element URL + offer id + customer data for a paid plan; the client opens the Fungies overlay checkout (@fungies/fungies-js) with the returned payload (no server-issued redirect URL). Returns `{ checkoutUrl, offerId, customerEmail, customFields: { checkout_ref } }` — `checkout_ref` is an opaque single-use nonce minted per checkout; the webhook resolves it against server-side state to link the subscription to the account. It carries no meaning on its own. Session-auth only (web flow). Rejects with 409 `already_subscribed` when the account already holds an active/trialing/past_due/scheduled_cancel subscription (the client should open the portal instead). Ships dark: returns 503 `billing_disabled` when billing is off.

200.description: Fungies checkout-element URL + offer id + customer data for the client-side overlay

503.description: Billing disabled (`billing_disabled`) or enabled with an incomplete offer/checkout-url mapping (`billing_misconfigured`)

post.description: Return the static Fungies customer-portal URL (magic-link login, env-configured) for the signed-in user to self-manage their subscription (change card, view invoices). The portal is a static, magic-link page, so this endpoint makes no provider call. Rate-limited per user (`billing_portal`, own hourly budget). 404 `no_subscription` if the account has no subscription with a stored customer id; 503 `billing_misconfigured` if billing is enabled but no portal URL is configured.

503.description: Billing disabled (`billing_disabled`) or enabled with no portal URL configured (`billing_misconfigured`)

post.description: Preview a self-serve plan change without committing it. The payment provider exposes no proration-preview call, so it is never contacted here — `immediateCharge`/`immediateCredit`/`nextBilledAmount`/`currencyCode` are always `null`, and `nextBilledAt` is always the current subscription's period end. A 200 means the change is possible and would apply immediately; the two refusals carry their own codes (400 `downgrade_not_offered`, 400 `interval_change_not_supported`) and are checked here for the same reason they are checked on commit — so the UI never opens a confirm dialog for a change that cannot happen. Rate-limited per user (`billing_plan_preview`, own hourly budget, more generous than the mutating plan-change endpoint since this one is read-only). 404 `no_subscription` if the account has no active-ish subscription; 409 `cancel_scheduled` if the subscription already has a cancellation scheduled (measured 2026-09-02: an accepted plan change does NOT clear the cancellation on the provider's side, so the subscription would still end on its original date - plan changes are blocked outright rather than leaving a billed-but-still-cancelled account); 400 `same_plan` if the target offer equals the current one.

200.description: Preview figures (money fields always null — see description)

400.description: Invalid plan/interval, or target equals current plan (`same_plan`)

503.description: Billing disabled (`billing_disabled`) or enabled with an incomplete offer mapping (`billing_misconfigured`)

post.description: Change the signed-in user's plan. A change may move the tier, never the interval, and never downward. An upgrade (resolved from `tierRank`: docs=api=1, pro=2) calls Fungies' `subscriptions/{id}/update` immediately with `create_prorations`; a lateral move (docs↔api, same rank and price) calls `update` immediately with `none` (no charge). Both are live when the call returns, so the response carries no effective date. 400 `downgrade_not_offered` for a move to a lower tier (owner decision: downgrades are not offered; cancelling remains available). 400 `interval_change_not_supported` for any monthly↔annual change in either direction — a subscription's billing interval is fixed for its lifetime and the provider refuses to change it (measured 2026-08-26/27). Rate-limited per user (`billing_plan_change`, reuses the checkout endpoint's hourly limit). 404 `no_subscription` if the account has no active-ish subscription; 409 `cancel_scheduled` if the subscription already has a cancellation scheduled (measured 2026-09-02: an accepted plan change does NOT clear the cancellation on the provider's side, so the subscription would still end on its original date - plan changes are blocked outright rather than leaving a billed-but-still-cancelled account); 400 `same_plan` if the target offer equals the current one.

400.description: Invalid plan/interval, or target equals current plan (`same_plan`)

503.description: Billing disabled (`billing_disabled`) or enabled with an incomplete offer mapping (`billing_misconfigured`)

post.description: Fungies webhook receiver. Public, no auth — protected by HMAC-SHA256 signature verification over the raw request body (`x-fngs-signature` header, `sha256_<hex>`). Idempotent on the event id (`id`, which also carries a separate `idempotencyKey` field): duplicate deliveries return `skipped_duplicate`. A signature/parse failure and a processing failure both respond 500 so Fungies retries — they're indistinguishable from the outside, so there's no separate 4xx for a bad signature. Not called by API consumers; documented for completeness.

500.description: Signature verification / payload parse failure, or a processing error — Fungies retries (`processing_error`)

post.description: Grant the signed-in user a fourteen-day Pro trial, started by this explicit call rather than at signup. No card, no payment provider — the trial is a tier grant with its own end date in our own database (Charter §6: the DB is the single source of truth for a plan either way), and `users.tier` is recomputed through the same `recomputeAndApplyTier` every billing event goes through, so a trial can never disagree with a subscription about which tier wins. A daily cron (`cron/expire-trials.ts`) re-triggers that same recompute once `endsAt` passes, for accounts that touch no other billing event in the meantime. Refused with 409 and one of four codes: `trial_already_used` (this address, in its normalised form — case, `+tag`, and Gmail dots collapsed — already had one, including under a different account sharing that form), `has_subscription` (an active-ish paying subscription needs no trial), `already_entitled` (a manually-granted `ultra` account already outranks the trial tier), `email_unverified`. Rate-limited per user (`trial_start`, own hourly budget) — the unique index on the normalised address already caps successful starts at one per address for life, so this only bounds repeated failed/probing calls.

§ 312k BGB cancellation-button declaration. Public, no auth, no CAPTCHA — the law requires this to be reachable without any hurdle. Always returns 200 on a structurally valid body, even when no account matches the given email: the declaration is legally received the moment it's accepted. An ordinary termination against a matched account with an active-ish, billing-enabled subscription and a requested date within the current billing period is cancelled with Fungies immediately (`autoExecuted: true`); every other case is stored for manual follow-up and the operator is notified (if `CANCELLATION_NOTIFY_EMAIL` is configured).

400.description: Validation error (e.g. missing reason for an extraordinary termination)
